## 2. The story format (same for every chapter)
Six scenes. The narrator reads each scene's caption; scene tabs, Next, and Play all narrate.
1. **Normal life** — meet the hero doing something they care about (mood `happy`).
2. **The problem** — something goes wrong because of the risky habit/concept (`tone: "trouble"`, a short `flash` of `surprise` then `sad`, or `thinking` where sad would be wrong).
3. **Help / understanding** — a trusted adult, teacher or the hero works out *why* it happened (`thinking`).
4. **Your turn (the task)** — `interactionScene: 3`. Narration pauses at the end of this scene until the learner completes the chapter's task (see §5). While solved the hero shows `solvedMood` (default `happy`).
5. **The deeper lesson** — the safe habit, with the correct terms for the class level (`happy` or `thinking`).
6. **A happier ending** — hero is okay, one-line takeaway, then "Your turn: …" leading into practice (`tone: "resolved"`, `happy`).
Never blame the victim. The story must feel like a story (feelings, stakes, a person), not a quiz with a mascot.

## 3. Difficulty grows with the class
| | Class 3–4 (lower) | Class 5 (middle) | Class 6–7 (upper) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Caption words per scene | 30–45 | 40–52 | 45–62 |
| Total narration | ~80–95 s | ~95–115 s | ~110–135 s |
| Language | short sentences, one rule, concrete | explains *why*; names the real term once ("this is called …") | realistic stakes, technical vocabulary used correctly, nuance ("one clue alone doesn't prove it") |
| Mid-story task | one tap/drag step with a tempting wrong choice | 2–3 decisions; feedback says *why* | investigate evidence / trace logic; justify, not guess |
| Speech bubble | ≤ 8 words | ≤ 10 words | ≤ 12 words |
Status line under the name: ≤ 4 words ("Feeling upset", "Checking the clues").

### World component contract
`World` stays mounted for the whole story, so keep the task's state inside it (like `selected` in the reference). Props: `scene, playing, elapsed, solved, markSolved, hint, setHint, reduced`. Wrap scene content in `<SceneSwap scene={scene} reduced={reduced}>` so every chapter transitions identically. Use `elapsed` + `playing` to reveal items in step with the narration (like the reference's recovery steps). Honour `reduced` (no motion). For the task scene: wrong/tempting choice → `setHint("…why…")`, never solves; correct completion → call `markSolved()` once; after `solved`, disable the task controls and show the finished state when the learner revisits the scene.

### Kit classes (import `k from "../story-player.module.css"`)
`k.device` (+ `data-dim`) / `k.deviceBar` / `k.deviceArt` (add your own class for a background image) / `k.deviceFoot` / `k.badge` / `k.alert` / `k.success` — a phone, tablet, game or app screen.
`k.panel` — cream explanation/task card; `k.panel > small` or `k.note` — small print.
`k.step` (+ `data-active`) — steps that light up with the narration.
`k.bank` — row of choice buttons (`aria-pressed` = used, `data-trap="true"` = tempting wrong choice).
`k.sceneContent .hint` → use `className={k.hint}` on a `<p aria-live="polite">`; `k.actions` — button row; `k.primary` — primary button; `k.fitIn` — little "fits in" animation.

Build real-looking screens with React + CSS + `lucide-react` icons + `motion/react`: incoming-call screens, video calls, SMS/chat threads, pop-ups, email clients with raw headers, social feeds, app permission sheets, UPI payment screens, code/pseudocode consoles, flowchart boards, robot command strips, datasets/photo grids, sorting bins. Existing illustrations you may use (in `public/cyber-missions/`, 16:9): `morning-room.webp` (kid's bedroom, school bag, shoes), `pattern-station.webp` (Cyberpur station with a smiling tram on tracks), `bookshop-payment.webp` (desk with books, tablet and phone), `engineering-lab.webp` (school maker lab: robot cleaner, hand-wash station prototype, blueprints), `safe-call-desk.webp` (study desk at dusk with a glowing phone — good for call scams), `fairground-vault.jpg` (Cyberpur fair at night), dog photos `dog-golden.jpg`, `dog-indie.jpg`, `dog-pug.jpg` (credits already in ASSET-CREDITS.md). `moonbase-story.webp` belongs to Rohan's chapter — don't reuse it.
No external URLs, CDNs, fonts, images or new npm packages. No real brands, banks, apps, people or real-looking phone numbers. Fictional places use "Cyberpur". Fictional domains end in `.example` (reserved, can never be real), e.g. `office.cyberpurschool.example` vs lookalike `cyberpur-school-office.example`. Fictional numbers look like `+91 00000 12345`. Mark examples as examples ("Example only", "Pretend call").
Motion: purposeful and short (≤ 300 ms UI, ease-out), `transform`/`opacity` only, nothing flashing faster than 3×/s, everything static under `reduced`.

## 6. Narration (same voice as Rohan)
Write captions to be *heard*: short sentences, natural rhythm, contractions, no symbols. If the spoken form differs from the on-screen caption, add `speech`: "OTP" → "O T P", "UPI" → "U P I", "PIN" → "pin", "CBI" → "C B I", "₹2,000" → "two thousand rupees", "1930" → "nineteen thirty" (as the helpline is said) or "one nine three zero", "cybercrime.gov.in" → "cybercrime dot gov dot in", "≥" → "greater than or equal to", "n log n" → "n log n", "Wi-Fi" → "wifi". Keep `speech` and `caption` saying the same thing.
Generate: `/Users/dipeshkumar/Documents/Codex/2026-09-27/do-u/work/piper-env/bin/python scripts/story-narration.py <slug>` (queues automatically; ~70 s once it starts). It writes the mp3 and fills every scene's start/duration + total. Re-run whenever any caption/speech changes. Check the total against §3.

## 8. Content rules (accuracy matters; this is for real schools in India)
- Trusted adult for every age; never tell a child to handle a scam alone or to confront a scammer.
- Report cyber fraud in India: call **1930** (National Cyber Crime Helpline) quickly if money was lost, and **cybercrime.gov.in**.
- OTP/PIN: no genuine bank, company, courier or government office asks for your OTP, PIN or password. Hang up and call the number printed on the card, bill or official app yourself.
- UPI: a PIN is only ever entered to **pay/send** money; you never need a PIN or a scan to **receive**. To receive, share *your own* QR/UPI ID. Read "Pay ₹…" on the screen.
- "Digital arrest" is not a real legal procedure. Police/CBI never arrest anyone over a video call, never demand secrecy, never ask for money to "clear" a case. End the call, tell family, report to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in.
- Voice cloning: a familiar voice is not proof. Use an agreed **family passphrase** and call back on a saved number.
- Deepfakes: artefacts (blinking, lip-sync, lighting, edges) are clues, not proof; confirm through an official source before sharing.
- Passwords: long passphrases, a different one for every account, two-step verification with an adult, a password manager or a paper list kept safe at home by a parent. Data breaches can happen even when you did nothing wrong.
- AI: machines follow programs and learn from examples; biased/incomplete data → unfair or wrong results; humans must check.
- Never ask the learner to type real personal data. Pretend data only.
